newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Sec denies compensation report.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Sec denies compensation report.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Wednesday denied a newspaper report which said the Japanese brokerage had been questioned by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) on suspicion of having compensated a corporate customer for losses.
The Hokkaido Shimbun, a regional daily, said on Wednesday that Nomura was suspected of having paid compensation of up to several hundred million yen to the customer.
Nomura's public relations office said in a statement it was not true that a Nomura executive had been questioned by the SESC and there were no such deals as reported by the paper.
The newspaper quoted the SESC and industry sources as saying that one of Nomura's corporate customers placed futures orders in Singapore markets through Nomura in 1994.
These deals resulted in a loss of several hundred millions of yen and Nomura tried to offset this loss by raising profits through trading shares for the customer, the paper said without elaborating.
Nomura said, however, that an internal investigation by the brokerage showed that neither the Singapore futures deal nor the ensuing compensation cited in the newspaper had taken place.
Nomura shares dipped due to the Hokkaido Shimbun report, but the downside risk for the shares was limited, market sources said.
By 0425 GMT, Nomura's shares were bid at 1,910 yen while the asking price was 1,920. The price briefly fell to 1,890 yen in the morning, down 50 from Tuesday's close.
